competition.title: Foss Forge 2.0
competition.details:
What Is FOSS FORGE?:

  • Join FOSS Forge 2.0 Whatsapp Community: https://chat.whatsapp.com/Dl6kisUVWmeHjSNH4bhVIW?s=cl&p=a&mlu=4&ilr=4
  • FOSS FORGE 2.0 is a competitive open-source event organized by UFC (USAR FOSS Club) at the University School of Automation & Robotics, GGSIPU East Delhi Campus.
  • But this is not a traditional hackathon.
  • Instead of giving everyone the same problem statement, FOSS FORGE gives you a pool of real-world challenges from open-source projects, non-profit organizations, communities, and technical partners. You choose what you want to solve, compete with others working on similar challenges, and earn points, rewards, and prizes based on what you accomplish.
  • Some challenges may ask you to build a tool that a non-profit currently needs. Others might be a CTF, bug bounty, debugging challenge, automation task, AI/ML problem, frontend or backend challenge, or something completely different.
  • There are no fixed tracks. The challenge you pick becomes your track.

Event Details:

  • Venue: University School of Automation & Robotics, GGSIPU East Delhi Campus, Delhi
  • Dates: 21–22 October 2026
  • ₹5,00,000+ cash prize pool
  • Sponsor-backed rewards, goodies and developer credits
  • Real-world open-source and community challenges

How FOSS FORGE Works:

1. Forge Your Rank:

  • The event begins with a competitive online quiz covering open source, Git, GitHub, programming, technology, and developer ecosystems.
  • Your performance determines your position on the leaderboard.
  • And your rank actually matters.
  • A better rank gives you an advantage when the challenge pool opens, so being fast, strategic, and knowing what you are capable of can make a real difference.

2. Choose Your Challenge:

  • Once the challenge pool opens, you can explore the available problems and decide what you want to take on.
  • These are not traditional GitHub issues.
  • A challenge could look something like: A non-profit organization needs a tool to automate a repetitive workflow. Build it, meet the requirements, and earn the points or rewards attached to the challenge.
  • Or: A repository has a security vulnerability. Find and responsibly report it within the given time limit to earn the associated points and rewards.
  • Or: A CTF challenge goes live at a specific time. Solve it before the deadline and compete for the top position.
  • Every challenge can have its own difficulty, time limit, scoring system, perks, and rewards.
  • Some may reward implementation.
  • Some may reward speed.
  • Some may reward finding the best solution.
  • Some may simply reward solving something nobody else could.
  • You choose what to compete for.

3. Forge & Ship:

  • Once you've chosen a challenge, it's time to work on it.
  • Depending on the challenge, you might need to build a complete tool, fix a technical problem, solve a CTF, find a vulnerability, automate a workflow, improve an existing system, or create something from scratch.
  • You'll work with real technologies and real requirements. You'll need to understand the problem, make technical decisions, build your solution, test it properly, and submit your work before the deadline.
  • Your submission may be evaluated on factors such as:
  • Technical quality · Correctness · Complexity · Impact · Completeness · Originality · Engineering practices
  • The best solutions earn their place on the final leaderboard.

The Challenges:

  • FOSS FORGE is designed so that there isn't just one way to compete.
  • You might find yourself working on:
  • Building a tool for a non-profit or community
  • Bug hunting and debugging
  • CTFs and security challenges
  • Bug bounty-style challenges
  • AI/ML challenges
  • Automation and developer tooling
  • Frontend or backend engineering
  • Documentation and developer experience
  • Open-source project improvements
  • Other technical challenges designed specifically for the event
  • Each challenge comes with its own requirements and rewards.
  • That means you don't need to be good at everything. Find the challenge that suits you and go after it.

Real Problems. Real Contributions:

  • The goal of FOSS FORGE isn't to create another pile of projects that gets abandoned after a hackathon.
  • Many of the challenges are based on actual needs from organizations, communities, and open-source projects.
  • The thing you build could become a real tool.
  • The bug you find could help secure a project.
  • The automation you create could save someone hours of work.
  • The contribution you make could continue being used long after the event ends.
  • You're not just building for judges. You're solving something that someone actually needs.

What You Can Expect:

  • Competitive opening quiz
  • Live leaderboard
  • A pool of real-world challenges
  • Time-bound competitions and challenges
  • Open-source and technical problem solving
  • Multiple technologies and domains
  • Mentorship and community interaction
  • Challenge-based scoring and evaluation
  • ₹5,00,000+ cash prize pool
  • Sponsor goodies, premium tools and developer credits
  • Recognition for high-impact contributions

Who Can Participate?:

  • Whether this is your first contribution or you've been working with open source for years, there's something for you.
  • Developers, AI/ML enthusiasts, security enthusiasts, competitive programmers, designers, students, makers, and anyone who enjoys solving technical problems are welcome.
  • You don't need to know every framework or every tool.
  • You just need to be willing to look at a problem, figure things out, and build a solution.

This Isn't A Hackathon:

  • At a normal hackathon, you're given a problem and told to build something.
  • At FOSS FORGE, you choose the problem.
  • You might build something for a non-profit.
  • You might win a CTF.
  • You might find a security bug.
  • You might ship an automation tool.
  • You might solve a problem nobody else managed to crack.
  • There is no single path to winning.
  • Find the challenge. Claim your shot. Forge the solution. Ship it.

FOSS FORGE 2.0 2026:

  • Find it. Forge it. Ship it.
  • Open source isn't something you just watch.
  • It's something you get your hands dirty with.

Stay Connected:

  • Join the official event group for event links, announcements, challenge updates and important information.

USAR FOSS Club Community:

  • Join the wider USAR FOSS Club community to stay connected with open-source activities, events, discussions and opportunities.
  • Join our Community: www.fossclub.tech/dashboard

FOSS FORGE / UFC:

  • Website: fossclub.tech

Issues can range from bugs and feature requests to documentation, automation, frontend, backend, AI/ML, and everything in between.

There are no fixed tracks.

Each issue is its own challenge.

Understand the problem, evaluate its complexity, and decide which one is worth taking on.

details.display_text:
Participate in coding contests hosted on Unstop.Now the real work begins.

Dive into the repository, understand the codebase, reproduce the issue, design your solution, write the code, test it, and prepare your contribution. Participants will work through an actual open-source workflow involving Git, GitHub, pull requests, testing, documentation, and collaboration.

You're not building a demo just for the judges.

You're building a contribution that can actually be used.
